assumptions: The brief's 'forecast half is untouched' is read as scoping the containment refusal to a DECLARED forecast (a typed --write, or handoff's reading-plan forecast); the include-set default forecast is governed by the read-side explicit-naming key instead. Rationale: a bare pack's defaulted forecast is ['.'], which covers any checkpoint by containment — evaluating that same include set under both keys would refuse every bare pack and defeat the session's ratified goal. Flagged first in notes.md for ratification.

The waiver stamp (checkpoint: null + checkpoint_waived) is scoped to {sid}-bearing bases; a read-only pack under a LITERAL base keeps stamping {path, sha256} as it has since v0.3.28 (the existing test pins it, the committed oracle exists, and 'the per-session checkpoint' is the brief's own wording).

A {sid} base with no static directory prefix (e.g. '{sid}.sh' at repo root) has no computable auto-exclusion basis; that degenerate shape keeps the pre-v0.4.9 containment refusal on the read side rather than gaining a wildcard exclusion, so the oracle cannot ship silently.
judgment_calls: bin/bale_report.py shipped as out-of-forecast drift: the read-side refusal's diagnosis/remedy text lives there, and the old text ('narrow this pack with --include paths that do not cover the checkpoint') became wrong under explicit-naming semantics — every refusal must name its real remedy.

Under --allow-checkpoint-in-scope, the read-half ADMISSION keys on containment (would the bytes ship with auto-exclusion off?) while the flag-less REFUSAL keys on explicit naming — this is what keeps 'the admission stamps exactly as today' true for the broad-include maintenance pack.
New per-sid tests live in a PerSidFixture base class split out of PerSidCheckpointE2ETest so the new classes don't re-run the S7 tests through inheritance.
The full 423-test suite is gated behind validation.sh --slow (TARBALL.md 7.6): the default run is ~40s, the slow leg ~105s; both were observed green.
